sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on the English Penn Treebank does Character-Aware Neural Language Models report for the proposed character-aware LSTM language model?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports 78.9 for the large proposed model (LSTM-Char-Large) and 92.3 for the small proposed model (LSTM-Char-Small) on the English Penn Treebank test set; predictions are made at the word level.

sub_questions.q: Does Character-Aware Neural Language Models report the Penn Treebank perplexity as a single model or with dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning?
sub_questions.answer: The reported Penn Treebank perplexities are single-model results. Ensembles are explicitly excluded; no dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, or fine-tuning Penn Treebank results are reported in the provided text.
sub_questions.quote: While lower perplexities have been reported with model ensembles [2012], we do not include them here as they are not comparable to the current work.

sub_questions.q: Which baselines and baseline perplexities does Character-Aware Neural Language Models list for the English Penn Treebank?
sub_questions.answer: Baselines listed in Table 3 are LSTM-Word-Small 97.6 (5m), LSTM-Word-Large 85.4 (20m), KN-5 141.2 (2m), RNN 124.7 (6m), RNN-LDA 113.7 (7m), genCNN 116.4 (8m), FOFE-FNNLM 108.0 (6m), Deep RNN 107.5 (6m), Sum-Prod Net 100.0 (5m), LSTM-1 82.7 (20m), and LSTM-2 78.4 (52m).
sub_questions.quote: As another baseline, we also train two comparable LSTM models that use word embeddings only (LSTM-Word-Small, LSTM-Word-Large).

sub_questions.q: How does the large proposed character-aware model compare with the listed Penn Treebank baselines and state of the art?
sub_questions.answer: LSTM-Char-Large 78.9 is on par with the best listed baseline, LSTM-2 78.4, while having approximately 60% fewer parameters (19m vs 52m); it outperforms the other listed baselines and the paper's word-level LSTM baselines.
sub_questions.quote: our large model is on par with the existing state-of-the-art (Zaremba et al. 2014), despite having approximately 60% fewer parameters.

sub_questions.q: How does the small proposed character-aware model compare with the listed Penn Treebank baselines?
sub_questions.answer: LSTM-Char-Small 92.3 outperforms LSTM-Word-Small 97.6 and other NLMs of similar size, but it is worse than LSTM-Char-Large 78.9, LSTM-Word-Large 85.4, LSTM-1 82.7, and LSTM-2 78.4.
sub_questions.quote: Our small model significantly outperforms other NLMs of similar size, even though it is penalized by the fact that the dataset already has OOV words replaced with < unk >

sub_questions.q: Do highway-layer settings affect the Penn Treebank perplexities reported for the proposed character-aware models?
sub_questions.answer: Yes. The main small model uses one highway layer (92.3) and the main large model uses two highway layers (78.9). Ablations show large model perplexities of 84.6 without highway layers, 79.7 with one highway layer, and 78.9 with two highway layers; small model values are 100.3, 92.3, and 90.1 respectively.
